spec_match.rationale: Every field, tag, enum and UI string in the composer is sourced: OnFileDownloadedEnterpriseConnector.yaml (service_provider, enable/url_list/tags, block_until_verdict, default_action), kDlpTag/kMalwareTag and FinalContentAnalysisResult::FORCE_SAVE_TO_CLOUD from connectors/core/common.h, danger types 24/25, EVENT_RESULT_FORCED_SAVE_TO_CLOUD = 8, and the grd shelf strings.

interactive.rationale: Selects, radios and a checkbox drive both a live connector-config preview and a step-by-step narrated journey; switching action or destination rewrites both outputs immediately.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises a composer with a narrated journey down to enum values, explicitly labelled an illustration — the page does exactly that, with the illustration banner above the fold.

edge_cases.rationale: All four actions (audit/warn/block/enforce) produce distinct journeys, both destinations map to their distinct danger types, and the block_until_verdict=0 branch narrates the enforcement race honestly.

references.rationale: Links the ChromeStatus entry, the policy definition on chromeenterprise.google, and the Chromium source file for the result enum; each journey step carries its own source path.

conformance.rationale: Covered by the feature-level suite; the enforcement contract this page illustrates is recorded there as a manual/blocked assertion rather than a fake executable check, which matches this page's illustration-only framing.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: default journey rendered (7 steps), destination switch to OneDrive rewrote the danger-type step to FORCE_SAVE_TO_ONEDRIVE (= 25), Block action produced 5 steps and disabled the destination select, switching back re-enabled it; zero console errors; desktop and 360x740 screenshots read; a 110px narrow-viewport overflow found in the journey list was fixed (overflow-wrap: anywhere) and re-measured at 0px.

telemetry_health.rationale: demo-telemetry.js loaded deferred; showcaseTelemetry.assert('rule-journey-rendered') fires on every recompose with action/tag/hold detail.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, the 'new in 155' badge is accent-blue on ivory (AA), fieldsets/legends styled within the system, config pre scrolls internally.

accessibility.rationale: Native fieldset/legend grouping, every select and input has an explicit label (automated scan found zero unlabelled controls), journey detail is an aria-live output, the destination select is disabled only while the config comment shows 'destination: (not applicable)' explaining why.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x2000: single-column form collapse via auto-fit grid, 0px horizontal overflow after the journey-wrap fix, 44px control heights, config block scrolls in place.

openQuestions.title: Cite the Chrome Enterprise 155 release notes once published in fetchable form
openQuestions.detail: The admin-console side (rule action name and destination picker wording) is currently grounded in the ChromeStatus rollout description and Chromium source. The Chrome Enterprise release notes page (support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/7679408) renders via JS and yielded no greppable content at build time. When the 155 notes are published and reachable, quote the console wording verbatim and add the link to the references.

guidanceConsulted.query: aria-live status log region for async events
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer native form elements with explicitly associated labels; use fieldset/legend for grouping; announce dynamic changes through a single polite live region.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All controls are native select/input/label with for/id association inside fieldsets with legends; only the journey summary output is aria-live so recomposition announces once instead of per-step.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP unlabelled-control scan returned []; journey re-render exercised across actions and destinations.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible file download links and user feedback
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Do not present state a user cannot act on as if it were interactive; disabled controls need visible context for why.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The destination select is disabled for non-cloud actions while the adjacent config preview prints 'destination: (not applicable)', giving a visible, textual reason.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP run: destination disabled=true under Block with the comment rendered, re-enabled under Enforce cloud storage.

summary: A policy-anatomy composer for a feature whose entire surface is an admin console: real schema fields, real enum values, real UI strings, and a prominent this-is-an-illustration banner. Interactivity, labelling and both viewport classes verified over CDP in headless Chromium 141; one narrow-viewport overflow was found and fixed during verification.
